I have a few questions about the design of the file with docs#Hindman.FP.

  • Are there any specific reasons to use docs#Stream' instead of Nat -> M?
  • Are there reasons to introduce a custom predicate FP instead of using something like (fun s : Finset Nat => Finset.prod s f) '' {s | s.Nonempty}?
  • The file abuses the defeq Set M = M -> Prop. Which way should I resolve this abuse?

CC: @David Wärn @Johan Commelin

I haven't inspected this particular formalisation, but I'm familiar with the informal proof here, and I agree that your second point is valid. The abuse is used to define FS and FP, so you could either make the auxiliary inductive definition M -> Prop and build the set from that (since the set is what we care about) or refactor to the non-inductive definition. Either would be mathematically sensible; I think the second would be more idiomatic.

Probably I used docs#Stream' and this inductive definition of FP because to me it made it clearer how the proof will proceed (using the basic API of Stream' and induction on FP). But in retrospect it would probably have been better to write this more idiomatically and less idiosyncratically.
